answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independently sampled, randomly assigned peers verify fabricated work or collusive attestations. Because reputation and future access are tied to the locked deposit, minting thousands of identities does not create free influence: a sybil farm must spread substantial capital across them and risks losing it on detection. An onyx-backed sonnet task paid in nectar could be one test job, not proof of personhood.
